yeah, Jesus Christ, dude. You need to stop. If you wanna actually be a trader, and you're hardcore serious that that's what you wanna be when you grow up, then sim trade. Stay in the simulator, trading whatever strategy without worrying about PnL or the sim balance just to learn the technicals until you're consistently profitable. Like at least a profit factor of 2 for like 90 days. And then don't go live until you've doubled the sim account from that point on, trading like you would a real account.

Also, don't allow yourself to actively trade with your net worth. Never leave a meaningful amount of your net worth in a trading account. Once you're ready to go live, open up a separate trading account with the minimum amount needed to trade your strategy. Not "how to trade" books, but biographies and memoirs, and books on trading psychology. The Market Wizards series, Reminiscences of a Stock Operator, everything by Mark Douglas, Best Loser Wins, Pit Bull, etc.

You got extremely lucky. Phenomenally lucky. By doubling down and doubling down, adding to a loser, you did the financial equivalent of putting a revolver to your head and pulling the trigger six times, and every time the bullet was a dud. Do not ever do anything like that again.
